lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.34 - A Look and learn

details: Look and learn helps students recognise key vocabulary and sentence structures by showing how nouns change with -s and -es in a clear table. It reinforces correct grammar and prepares students for writing and speaking activities.
Look for students demonstrating understanding of the grammar in the table, correctly identifying singular and plural forms, and showing awareness of -s and -es patterns.
“We’re having a fruit and vegetable party with enough for everyone! Look at the table to see who to invite!”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.34 - B. Look and write

details: Look and write develops writing and comprehension by helping students practise plurals. Students complete the correct plural forms by linking the pictures to the words, reinforcing spelling and vocabulary.
Look for correct plural forms, neat handwriting, accurate spelling, and students using the singular form and picture cues carefully.
“Oh dear! Some of the fruit and vegetables are trying to sneak into our party without the right endings! Can you help them by adding an ‘s’ or ‘es’?”

lessonPlan.topic: Phonics Book p.118 - A Listen and circle

details: Listen and circle continues checking beginning-sound recognition. Students listen for the target word, match its first sound to the correct letter choice, and show understanding by neatly circling the right option.
Look for careful listening, mostly accurate letter choices, clear circling, and steady pencil control,
“These words want to join our party too! We just need to work out what their beginning sounds are.. Can you listen and help?”

lessonPlan.topic: p.120 - C Circle words that start with d or k

details: Circle words that start with d or k develops students’ ability to recognise initial sounds in print. Students scan the speech bubbles and captions, identify beginning letters, and show understanding by circling the correct words.
Look for accurate identification of d– and k–initial words, neat circling, and steady pencil control.
“That was such a fun party! There’s just one guest left. It’s an animal that starts with a /d/ sound. Can you guess what it is?”

lessonPlan.topic: p.120 - D Say the words that start with d or k

details: Say the words that start with d or k practices clear pronunciation of initial sounds. Students say each selected word aloud, reinforcing correct d/k sound production and building confidence with sound–letter links.
Look for clear initial sounds, confident repetition, audible distinction between d and k, and most students producing the target words accurately.
